A LITTLE FIELD GUIDE

A link. A little world. Yours.

Four small steps. No design degree required.

01

This is a practice space. Your design stays untouched.

Shortcuts & a few useful things

Click Next piece Shift + click goes back

Tab Focus a piece Enter or Space swaps it

Use Undo / Redo to experiment. Save project keeps your link, design choices, and motion settings in a file you can reopen.

New links, Remix, and scene-detail changes rebuild the small pieces. Palette changes keep your edits. The scenery around the QR never appears in a download.

Test your exported QR on real phones at the size you will use, including while an animation plays. Digital checks are not a camera-scan guarantee.

On your device.

QR encoding, illustration, digital checks, and file exports run in your browser. This app sends no link, caption, or artwork to a server.

There are no analytics, accounts, cookies, third-party fonts, or paid generation APIs. We do not save your links in local storage. Reloading clears the studio. Save project explicitly downloads a JSON file containing your destination and design choices onto your device; keep that file private when its destination is sensitive.

The exported QR encodes the website you enter, not a Squarekin redirect. Anyone scanning it can read that destination, so do not use a private or sensitive link unless you intend to share it.

Works offline, too.

Save this HTML file and open it in a desktop browser. All of the app's code, illustration tools, and optional soundtrack are bundled in the file. An original instrumental loop is included in this file. It attempts to play on arrival; when your browser requires interaction, it starts after your first click, tap, or keypress. Use the music button to pause at any time. It needs no streaming service and is not included in exports. Music and volume choices are kept only for this open page; they are not stored or added to saved projects.

VALIDATION

Digital checks

The illustrations deliberately change a budgeted part of the QR data. We sample four renderings, repair the sampled codewords, decode the destination, and verify parity. Every block must retain at least 25% of its theoretical error-correction capacity, and the reserved pattern centers and clear margin must pass.

These are fixed-grid render checks, not phone-camera tests.

The correction reserve is not a real-world reliability score. These checks do not test whether a camera can locate the code in a scene, nor perspective, glare, shadows, or printing. Scan a physical sample before producing a batch. A browser-native QR scan is also attempted when available. With QR motion on, additional frames are sampled across the loop. GIF exports check every final indexed frame; animated SVG and HTML exports sample 24 frames. This does not test every possible frame or camera exposure.

QR error correction: H · Four-module clear margin · Direct destination

Credits

Little Hours is an original, synthesized instrumental loop made for Squarekin: soft keys and warm ambient chords at 64 beats per minute. No third-party sound recordings or music streams are used.

QR encoding uses QRCode for JavaScript by Kazuhiko Arase, from qrcode-terminal 0.12.0. The studio UI, connected-contour illustration engine, codeword-budget planner, and fixed-grid Reed-Solomon decoder were built for this MVP.
